utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Registrar, could you kindly call the case, please, and good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, usual advisory, if there are problems with interpretation, please draw our attention straight away. Let me have a look. I think we are in full force today. Yes. And Prosecution, all right. Any preliminaries before we continue with the evidence? I see none. Mr. Ruez, bon jour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Welcome back. We are going to proceed with your testimony and you don't need to repeat your solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, it will be a usual day with the usual breaks of 25 minutes each.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, I guess we will just continue with General Mladic trying to get the APC out from the tree and we have about an hour and 20 minutes of this sort of video and then we'll get into the question and answer again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ruez, can you tell us where they are coming into now?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the south entrance of Srebrenica town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: On -- sorry, my screen just left, on 23.59.9.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, we are now at 25.02.6 and can you identify the person standing, well, according to the picture, to the left of this jeep vehicle, next to it?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This man is General Krstic at that time deputy to the commander of the Drina Corps who was General Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know the person in black holding the flag, do you know, has that person's unit been identified to you in the investigation?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was the man wearing black uniforms are members of the 10th sabotage detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And who told that to you?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Drazen Erdemovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. If we could continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: There is again we are at 25.27.9, and there has been a reference to Zile and Zivanovic. Do you see General Zivanovic in this portion?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at the edge of the frame.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, we are at 31.13.3, and can you identify the people first we see well, General Mladic, with his back to us, and who else do you recognise?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just behind him is Colonel Pandurevic. At the left of Colonel Pandurevic is Lieutenant Colonel Vujadin Popovic. He was also seen a few frames before, before 30.50, and at the left, totally at the left of the picture is General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, we are going to try to go back to that man. Okay, we are at 1.57.28.6. Do you recognise the person in camouflage to -- in the far left of the screen?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He has been identified as being Colonel Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not trying to say this is not Mr. Borovcanin but I have a problem with the way the question was posed. Do you recognise this man? I don't believe there is foundation for such a question. There is no record that the witness met Mr. Borovcanin ever in his life so I don't believe that it's a proper question to ask this witness, "Do you recognise this man?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: "Do you recognise the person in camouflage to the far left of the screen?" It's a perfectly legitimate question. Thank you. Go ahead. I don't see any basis for sustaining your objection. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, I know that it's a difficult picture but the person in the blue vest will be as you've now seen repeatedly in this movie. Can you identify that person?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He is a UN military observer, Major Kingori from Kenya.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record we are at 1 minute, 59 -- 1 hour, 59 minutes 39.5 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, can you just remind us who this person is in the forefront giving the interview?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And have you seen this video many times?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And does someone come walking up behind General Krstic during this interview?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You will have to stop on the good frame but, yes, indeed, Lieutenant Colonel Popovic is walking behind at some point.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And can you tell us -- I know the frame said this was Potocari 12 July but can you tell us just where this is? We will get a more precise indication by map and photo later in the trial but can you just tell us generally where this is?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: A bus is hiding the building behind but whether it will pass, one will see the blue structure. It's a location we call the blue building. I will pinpoint it on the map later on, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And we are at 2.03.08.4. And we'll try to stop it, well, when you tell us to stop it if you see Lieutenant Colonel Popovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Can you identify why you said stop? Who do you see where?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the right of the left ear of General Krstic, Lieutenant Colonel Vujadin Popovic is coming from the direction of the north towards the direction of the south.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And this is 2.04.05.9. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, this said SRT TV. Do you know what that means?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you -- well, I won't ask you to speculate but I think we all know who this is but can you tell us for the record? And it's at 2.05.57.1.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he can be recognised as being President Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, can you tell us what the significance of this Luke area is briefly?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the exit way from the Serb-held territory towards the Muslim-held territory at Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And from what you've learned in the investigation, who was -- who was taken here?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people who were bussed [Realtime transcript read in error, "burst"] out of Srebrenica were taken towards this area, and from there, they would walk by foot through the confrontation zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Roughly how far a walk was it through the confrontation zone to the Kladanj Muslim zone?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would assess approximately four kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record page 6, line 10, not the people who were burst out of Srebrenica, the people who were bussed out of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I should say we stopped for that explanation at about 02.13.30.3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. McCloskey. We can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, we saw the title of this clip but can you just give us a little more information on what this depicts, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the arrival at Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And these two men dressed in camouflage uniforms, do you know what units they belong to?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was later told that indeed they are UN soldiers and that the man at the left is Major Boering.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are at 2 hours 15 minutes 44.5 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We don't need to stop but just for the record, Mr. Ruez, can you tell which side film footage this is coming from? I know we've seen mostly Serb footage but is this different.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This cannot be Serb footage because this is Muslim-held territory close to Kladanj so it must be some Bosniak Muslim footage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before this part of the video started was RTL Speranza does that mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, at 2.17.58.2, this segment started off with BiH TV and mentioned the airport. Can you just tell us briefly the significance of the airport?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the first refugees arrived at Tuzla, the first place they were taken to was the air base. Some 6.000 to 8.000 refugees then settled on this base.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The title that began here at about 02.21.24.5 has been entitled the Petrovic footage. You briefly mentioned that yesterday. And can you just reiterate who Petrovic is and what this is about, just very briefly?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's a journalist from B92 Radio and he was present in the area at the time of the events.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did the investigation reveal there was any connection between him and Mr. Borovcanin in regarding to him, his film?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were driving in the same vehicle so they went to the same places.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And the video will speak for itself on that point, Your Honours, and we will deal with the specifics in much more detail later, and not with this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just a reminder for the record, what date is this? If you remember.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think it is July 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We don't need to stop anything but these initial shots that we've been seeing, what town have they been in and are continuing to be in.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this moment, this is Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And for the record, the shots that Mr. McCloskey is referring to are those immediately preceding 2 minutes -- 2 hours point 24 minutes point -- right up to the beginning of the -- this part of the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: At 2.25.49.1, the man in the middle with the beret, do you remember who he is?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. He's a UN soldier but I don't remember his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, the person in the centre wearing the blue vest, have you received any information about -- in the investigation, briefly, where that vest came from?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I think we are going just a little too far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Objection anticipated. Sustained. I think that was too much of a direct question. Mr. McCloskey, please rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you speak to a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can he give us any information about the man in the centre wearing the blue bullet-proof vest? And if he can say anything about that bullet-proof vest, let's leave it at that, unless you want to add further questions after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, that's my question. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the man in the middle is playing the role of the interpreter with the UN forces, and though his flak jacket is of blue colour, this is not material stolen to the UN. These flak jackets were given -- provided to members of the special police brigade while they were training at their centre in Jahorina and inside the flak jackets the inscriptions were written in Cyrillic so this is not material stolen to the UN, like it was in other situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And you received that information from one of the Serb soldiers?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Once we are at this because he seems to know enough about this subject matter, just imagine for a moment that the soldier next to -- next to him wore or was wearing one of the UN flak jackets, would you be able to tell the difference looking at both of them or would you be able to tell the difference only if you looked at the inside to see the inscription?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There would be absolutely no difference. One would have to look inside the flak jacket.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I think that's clear enough. Mr. McCloskey, you may proceed. I apologise for interrupting you again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: At 2.27.49.5, the person whose back is to us, I think we've seen a bit of a profile, can you, from what you've seen or what you know of this film, identify the person with his back to us?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There will be better frames, but as far as we know he's Colonel Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Again my timing wasn't very good but 2.28.25.9, the person again he's got his back to us to the left of the screen, who is that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, in between the two references you gave we could see him on several frames, Colonel Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And the black man in blue, who is that again?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: An UNMO, he's a major I spoke before about, Major Kingori.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Again, at 02.29.56.1, who can you recognise in this photograph and can you describe where they are?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this picture is taken just at the -- at the angling of the White House. At the left of the picture is Major Kingori and in the middle of the picture is Colonel Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And yesterday you mentioned about the Petrovic film and having some black parts or some cutout parts and then you also mentioned the B92 piece that is came in later and we'll get some sections coming up on that point soon, Your Honour, where I will stop but as I mentioned, this is a compilation that the Prosecution has put together and so you will see edits for targeted purposes. The Defence has all the full footages of all this. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let me just stop right there, if I could. We saw a big shell casing. Let me -- I'm sorry, Your Honours, we have now gone to this studio B segment and Mr. Ruez, can you orient us on why that segment comes in here the way it does?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume because this one is going to show the parts that were cut from the film.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. The segment that I missed getting, there was a house. We could see a bit of a house. Just before this at 2.30.19.2, which house it was?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go back a little bit. I think it can be done easily. I recognise Mr. Haynes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm afraid the answer that is coming when it's prefaced with the phrase, I assume, does not give me any confidence that this witness can actually give any evidence about this section of the film.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's see. I wouldn't anticipate as much as you are doing, Mr. Haynes but let's see. Yes. Let's finish this -- see this part again. And then we go to the next -- this is still the Petrovic part of the Petrovic footage, no?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the next one, which is from the -- that station, the other station, I forgot what.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: B92 station is also part of the Petrovic footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's proceed with this one first. We get to the next one and then you put your question, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This white goat, he's standing in front of a house. What house is he standing in front of?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You will have to advance a few frames but the so-called white house will be easily recognisable. The only thing is that the way the film is framed it will stop just under the balcony.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, the -- we don't see a very good picture of the balcony in this shot; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because the balcony is just at the top of the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And in the original Petrovic film, did we get a shot of the balcony?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Will we see a better shot in the B92 version?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we will.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And this has been stopped at 2.30.11.5 where we see things piled up in front of what Mr. Ruez has identified as the white house. Okay. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Ruez, we are at 02.30.40.8 and what is this a shot of?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is again a shot of so-called white house and men are sitting on the balcony.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. If we can continue just to play it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now we are back to the regular Petrovic video; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not so sure. I think this is a Dutch footage. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. This is indeed the Petrovic one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is Dutch footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: He's referring to 02.31.26 point --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, that's the end of this particular -- the Dutch footage. We go back to some more footage but I believe it's time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have a 25-minute break starting from now. For the record, the tape is stopped at 2 hours 36 point -- 36 minutes point 36 seconds point 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, for -- we can continue and for the record, the video resumes in the same position it was stopped before the break, namely at 2 hours, 36 minutes point 36 point 6 seconds. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, apparently we just have a little bit more of this section and then I believe we get to the more of the Petrovic video and I may not stop to identify Mr. Borovcanin at this point, unless the Court thinks they would like clarification on that but I think we've seen his face enough that maybe that hopefully won't have to take the time to do that but I'll leave that to Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is the Dutch footage, no? Still the Dutch footage?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, just for a few more seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I said it. I knew it. I said it for the record, basically.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, this section is entitled, "On the road." Can you tell us what road are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is the road that goes from Bratunac towards the intersection of Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And this particular scene, do you know -- can you just give us a rough description of where this is?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This should be on a meadow that we name Sandici meadow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And we'll just leave it play for a while. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we stop here at 02.54.07.5. We have changed areas. Do you know roughly where this area is we've got? We just went by some sandbag structure?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the limit of the Srebrenica enclave whether coming from the road that goes from Bratunac towards Potocari. More or less in between mid-distance between Bratunac and Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And which direction is this vehicle that the camera is in travelling?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this moment driving towards Potocari. This was the UN check-point marking a limit of the enclave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you remember the name of that place?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Stopping at 2.54.54.6, what direction are they going in if you know?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Potocari driving, towards Srebrenica town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we go back a bit to play that Studio B segment? But before we do I just want to ask Mr. Ruez a question or two. Mr. Ruez, we saw Studio B segment played in real time and then a slow motion piece. Can you tell us what we are seeing there, if you recognise the area?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is [indiscernible] that a strange place in the chronology of this video because this is no longer in the area of Potocari going towards Srebrenica. The segments you are showing at this moment show the hangar, the so-called warehouse very nearby Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And which direction is that -- is the vehicle or the camera going in?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the moment, it shows the warehouse of Kravica. The vehicle is driving from the direction of Konjevic Polje towards Bratunac. So the warehouse is at the right-hand of the vehicle. But again it's a very different area than the one of the previous footage and the one that is following now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's have a playback of both footages, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could start with the real time and then get the slow motion, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is Potocari. Now it jumps to the Kravica warehouse. This last picture was again in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Potocari. So who -- who sandwiched the Kravica part in between the Potocari shots?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not the one who edited this film, I cannot say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. I just wanted to make sure whether it was you or not in the first place. So this is not your editing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it is not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you haven't been able to find out whose editing it is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I never asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, the B92 footage just for your information came from -- originally from Mr. Borovcanin and about the same time a journalist got it as well, and we will be able to provide you some answers to those questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I won't put any further questions, then. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And that was just after Mr. Ruez's time here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, I notice that it can proceed but I notice that we have quite a stretch of footage now and we can -- those who can follow the Serbian conversation or words that are being spoken, but there are -- there is no translation and we are not receiving interpretation. Is what is being said important for you or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, it -- we have a transcript of this segment for you. It was not -- well, it's a long story about the difficulties of subtitling but it was not considered as crucial in the resources for subtitling ran out. We have now another system which we will see another -- in other videos but we do have a transcript so you will see this information as you could recognise perhaps some of the villages and I'm sure you would be interested in what they are saying and so I apologise for not having this done but we do have a transcript that goes along with this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I made the same note on 34:30 where the Muslims were in the woods I think it was captioned there was no translation of that column and I wonder if you may ask the Prosecutor if that's the same explanation there as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you've put the question and Mr. Ostojic has heard you. What's your position on that, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's the same answer and they've had that transcript for a long time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if there is any question, we will be able to give that to everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. President, we'll continue and I will endeavour to have a -- the new version of subtitling for those final portions and for the final exhibit. I think it would be better.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Ruez, we are going back now. We were going through, if you recall, our chronology, and I believe we need to start back where we I think you entitled it, "Bratunac." Go back, I believe, it's number 10. All right. Now, Mr. Ruez, what -- where does this fit into the chronology? What's the significance of your next photos?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The black arrow on this map indicates the movement that was made by the men held at the White House towards Bratunac town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. So let's -- and this is 10. Let's go to 11. And we see another US aerial image before us dated 12 July indicating Bratunac city. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And have you made these circles that we see on this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. At the top left of the picture is the direction coming from Potocari and the blue arrow points to a circle in the middle of the circle is a hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Can you -- if the blue is going towards Potocari, can you orient us and perhaps Ms. Stewart will help us with that little mouse thing. Where is the road going towards Konjevic Polje, if it can be seen?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Arrow should go to the left. To the top. More or less where the -- where the of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the D of "and", Bosnia and Herzegovina, where the D is, okay. This is the direction towards Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if we could just go down here, is that the road where the little hand it?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's a bit at the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And if we can now let's see how this thing focuses on this thing you've circled in blue. Okay. Now, can you tell us what -- I see -- we all see a building in the middle of the blue circle. Can you tell us what that is?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So, this is the so-called hangar in Bratunac where the first detainees were taken to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And what are the buildings around it? What have you learned from the investigation that the buildings around it are?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The other buildings will be used later. It's the so-called Vuk Karadzic school complex.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And do you know which one of those is actually the Vuk Karadzic school?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The in fact exactly where the blue arrow points to is the Vuk Karadzic school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And is there a gym attached to that school?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's a little bit hidden by the line of the blue circle but it is the structure that can be seen just behind the Vuk Karadzic school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is there a third building in that area that -- where you -- that you learned was significant?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But not for that day. The building that is bottom left of the hangar is the so-called old school, technical school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And that's where the little hand is now?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And the -- if we could go back, we also -- if we go to the left of the picture, we see some -- what look like -- can you tell us what those things are, those long white things that are all behind each other over by where the hand is?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: A line of buses waiting to drive towards Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And if we could just pan back up so we can get a good look at the town and according to the United States, this is 12 July 1995. And this is again image 11. If we can go to the next image, 12?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment let me stop you for one moment. Why does he conclude that those buses were waiting to drive towards Potocari and not, for example, to Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can answer that if we return to the picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The reason is that the vehicles are on a parking lot. Would they be driving towards Konjevic Polje and then towards Kladanj, they would be on the road that goes to the direction of Konjevic Polje. At this moment, many of them are on the parking place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. If we could go to the next one? And this is 12. A bit fuzzy but can you tell us what this is?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is an extract of a video film from helicopter showing Bratunac town and the yellow square marks the approximate location of the hangar and this shows that it's very close by of the middle of the town, centre of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 13, and what is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a ground photograph taken from this hangar. I would assess it was taken in summer 1997 and this is a photograph that was shown to a person who claimed having been detained there and who recognised the structure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I've let this go on. This is exactly -- this testimony is exactly the motion that we filed to address this situation. He's just nothing but giving speculation, the buses had to be going there because they are on a parking lot. He wasn't there in 1995. This last answer, for example, "I would assess it is taken in the summer of 1997."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perhaps he can explain why he makes that assessment. Yes, Mr. Ruez, why do you state that you make -- you assess that this was taken in summer of 1997?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First I must say that I am the person who took that photograph. We could not -- I did not go to Bratunac town in 1996. So we went on a mission there but I would not be able to say, to remember if it was in April or in June 1997.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think that resolves the issue that you raised Mr. Meek. Speculation is one way that you certainly cannot really refer to this part of the witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would agree that that last answer would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not speculation. MR. MEEK -- he gave the question to -- he gave to the last question presented to him, the answer. However, to go back to 12, go back to 13, and 11, I mean, it's going to be a continuing objection. I'll stay off my feet, Your Honours, but this is exactly what we didn't want to happen and I assumed this is what the Trial Chamber wasn't going to let happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This isn't speculation, Mr. Meek. Please proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I can assure you, Mr. Meek, when it's pure speculation we will stop the witness and Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to the next -- your next photograph, 14. This is a map and can you tell us what section of your materials you've entitled this extrication. What does this refer to as a lead-up to your next photographs?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a map of the area and the black arrow indicates the direction that the column took in order to reach the area of the intersection of Konjevic Polje, that's the asphalt road and then try to infiltrate the area as we know through Nerzuk.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to your first picture. This is 15. Can you tell us what this is a photo of and what this yellow line depicts?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The road at the bottom of the picture shows to the left the direction of Bratunac and to the right the direction of Konjevic Polje. The yellow arrow marks the approximate direction taken by the column. The goal of this photograph is to show how the terrain looks like in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 16. And can you explain what this depicts?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the intersection of Konjevic Polje is a huge hill, and this is from that hill that then the column had to cross the asphalt road. The asphalt road is marked with an a dotted line, bottom left going to the Konjevic Polje intersection and top right going to Nova Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bourgon first and Madam Fauveau after.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, I would like to know we have a picture here which is number 16 of 271 I would like to know where this picture -- what is the number of that picture in the Rule 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you answer that question, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This does not have a specific Rule 65 ter number. There are other pictures that do have 65 numbers that have part of this terrain but as I think I said yesterday, the one area that I found that was not as closely related to the 65 ter numbers was the area of the hills where the column went and these were issues that were brought up in the early part of the testimony and that -- so I thought that they are -- are relevant. Of course, these hills are the similar hills that we've just seen in the video but as I've stated before, and as I thought we put to rest yesterday, these do not have always precise identical photographs of what was on the 65 ter list but it's the same areas, the same places, same -- many of the same shots, different angles, different clarities, and I repeatedly asked if anyone felt surprised by any of the photographs they have had for two weeks, please let me know. No one has said a thing to me. I don't think anyone is surprised. I think this is purely obstruction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I really don't appreciate the comments that this is obstruction but nevertheless I will reply to this obstruction. This is not a matter of being surprised or not surprised. The matter is there are rules to be followed before the International Tribunal. It is the duty of the Trial Chamber to uphold these rules. In this case I have my colleague here who suddenly adds exhibit P2103. Mr. President, this is an exhibit that contains 271 pictures. This exhibit has never been added to the list of the exhibits the Prosecution intends to offer at trial. If they want to go beyond their original list of 2100 they have to seek leave from the Trial Chamber. This has never been done. Our objection, Mr. President, is simply that we have prepared this trial on the basis of 2100 exhibits. Now we have new exhibits. If my colleague cannot tell us exactly what number this exhibit is on this list, then I object that the exhibit even be used with this witness. There are reasons why we have rules before this International Tribunal. We can't just say, "They've had it for two weeks, they've had it for a long time." That doesn't help, Mr. President. There are rules to be followed and we kindly ask you, we respectfully ask the Trial Chamber to uphold the rules before this Trial Chamber -- before this Tribunal, meaning that if there is a new exhibit, they must seek leave to have this exhibit admitted, they must seek not admitted, sorry, they must seek leave to even present the exhibit so that we know exactly where we are going. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. McCloskey, do you want to respond to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have responded continually. I believe there was a ruling on this very issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I must raise an objection to the line of questions by Mr. McCloskey and also to the answers by the witness. We've heard already that he wasn't there in 1995. He doesn't know, he can't know, where the column was going, which was the hill through which the column went. If he wants to testify as to these facts, he must say where he has this knowledge from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think he can tell us that without any difficulties. In the meantime, let's discuss.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's start with Madam Fauveau's objection which we think can be resolved easily. Mr. Ruez, you have indicated routes here and streets and roads, indicating the route taken by various people that you referred to. On what do you base this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I base this knowledge on the numerous interviews that we had with people who walked along this path. I think even that during the video we just saw, I don't understand Serbo-Croatian language but I hear some man giving directions and this is the direction I hear from them being explained. We also have the records of the Bosnian army who indicate as having crossed this area. So more or less all the people who managed to escape from this area, in between Konjevic Polje and the enclave, all claim having gone through this area and mainly through this hill. We also have several witnesses who from that hill gave us indications that later enabled us to discover crime scenes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now going back to the other matter raised by Mr. Bourgon. Now, as I pointed out yesterday before Mr. Ruez started giving evidence, P02103, as is, as it is, is prone to raise problems in that it contains 271 images of crime scenes and maps, some of which I think you concede do not have 65 ter number. Legally, and procedurally, Mr. Bourgon is right when it comes to documents that have not been disclosed under the 65 ter Rules. So what we are going to do for the time being is that as we go along, when we identify these, they will be marked only for identification separately, and then ultimately we will decide on the P 02103, what's going to happen with it, because, as was explained by Mr. McCloskey before, the majority or the great majority of the images there do have a 65 ter meeting [sic]. So if they can be collected together and presented as one CD with new number, that is no big deal, and this definitely does not infringe the procedural rules that -- and evidentiary rules that we have. We would appreciate from the Defence benches and we thank you for having brought this up, Mr. Bourgon, any other images that will be shown on the screen as we go along, that you find difficulty in accepting because they do not have a 65 ter meeting -- 65 ter reference number, so if you can identify them for us, it will help us later on determine whether P 02103 should be included in the evidence as one whole or whether it should be eliminated from the records as an exhibit and the records would refer only to the various images that we would have seen in the meantime and which have a 65 ter or some other reference that would have been disclosed to you before. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, and I -- just to explain, I have made a distinction from documents and intercepts and photographs. The ground that we are seeing is so -- is covered by I would think 99.9 per cent of the images that have been provided to counsel. These -- they may be different angles, different dates, but it's the same basic place. Of course, when we are talking about a military document or an intercept, it's absolutely essential for 65 ter. I recall Your Honour saying that witnesses sometimes come and bring materials and Mr. Ruez no longer works here and that's what he's done. He's brought these materials with him in a better format really than our old format so I will endeavour absolutely to clarify this but that's -- and I also -- I've got it tell you, Mr. President, I was not aware that the -- that the -- the location of where the column is going is a contested issue. Had they mentioned that in their trial briefs or made an issue of it I would need 200 more witnesses but I don't think it is a contested issue and this adherence to this kind of adversarial system is something that this Tribunal has as you know has gotten away from for good reason. And that's all I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. McCloskey. Incidentally, part of your submissions are relevant for later consideration that we may need to make on whether there is any material prejudice to the rights of the Defence, particularly if you submit that these images from a different angle or in a different format had been previously submitted to the Defence but let's not discuss that. What you both need to understand is that in the real life of trials, we are going to come across fresh documents that sometimes are brought over by witnesses who have somehow dug them up or came across them, which were not available to the Prosecution before and which will become available during the testimony. I mean, of course, permission will have to be sought for the introduction of those documents in the records as exhibits, but this is something that is going to happen, happens in every trial, and it does, in a way, hinge also on one of the submissions made by Mr. McCloskey, namely that this is something that the witness has prepared for us, and which would not necessarily belong to those categories of documents that need necessarily be disclosed to you pursuant to Rule 65 ter. But let's not make a storm in a tea cup out of this issue because I don't think it deserves it and we will mark this particular as marked for identification and we will proceed. Yes, Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We take good note of the Trial Chamber's ruling. However, I'd like to point out that the difficulty that arises from this issue has a practical difficulty. As I've mentioned, we have prepared this case on the basis of 2100 exhibits. We are just trying to follow when we see a picture there to try and come up with what number it is so that we can go back to our comments. There is practical difficulties associated with that. It is by no means the intention of the Defence to try and be obstructive. We just try to have the possibilities and facilities to do our work. And right now every single of those pictures, not every single it's not true, for some we were able to say, Oh, yes this is Exhibit 1560, but for many of them we were not able to do that and that's the difficulty we have in following these proceedings. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Bourgon, but let me assure you that had it been the conviction of the Trial Chamber that you are being obstructive, we would not be intervening the way we are. We fully understand your problem and believe me it's not just your problem, it's also our staff's problem. It's also our staff's problem, and the same problem was brought to our attention before the witness started giving evidence and we are just for the time being playing it by the ear. We see how it develops. If it becomes too complicated then we will have to take certain measures to regulate the matter accordingly. The last thing we want is to put you or put ourselves in a position where we have too much of a confused situation or a confusing situation which would not let us proceed and base our judgement later on, on something which is easily identifiable. All right? Thank you. Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I'd noticed in the -- and of course we're in the first chair here. I've noticed the witness has been testifying from notes and I would ask the Chamber to enjoin him to give us a copy of the notes between the break, the next break, so we might look at what he's referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you looking, are you referring at notes, Mr. Ruez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. I have not one single note with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I'm not quite blind but I know he took it out of his breast pocket, he looked at it. There it is right there. I don't know what it is. Maybe they are not notes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the list provided to you by the Prosecution, the list of the witnesses which have numbers on them. This is not notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you satisfied with that, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Pardon me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you satisfied with his explanation?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I am satisfied with that explanation now that I see what it is. There, however, is a sticky note on the back of it. I don't know if he's referring to that or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's continue. Mr. McCloskey -- Mr. Ruez, you don't need, the Trial Chamber does not require any further explanations from you. It's satisfied with your word. Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You lost track. Same here. I think before you put your next question, let me just go back.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Maybe we should just go directly to cross-examination, Your Honour. But that's cheating. I'll go through. I think we are done with this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Bourgon, if it's nothing new, please sit down.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. President, it is something new. My colleague keeps doing this useless senseless and with all due respect stupid comments and we would like him to refrain from making such comments about the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Bourgon, Mr. McCloskey, I object myself to this unparliamentary kind of language. My dear counsel and Prosecutor, you have a good two, three years here in this trial. It's in everybody's interest, particularly your interest, to create and continue having an environment which is friendly, fair and which is conducive to a proper administration of justice and the continuation of the trial. If as has happened in other trials the environment becomes poisoned, if it becomes bitter, you will gain nothing out of it except that we will be required to intervene with a strong hand to make sure that the rules of ethics and the procedural rules are observed to the letter. At that point in time, there will be no longer flexibility. There will be no longer nice words like I'm saying now. So my suggestion to you is that you try your best not to exchange hard words or words which can stick in the back of your mind. Please try to cooperate one with the other, one side with the other, as much as you can, and keep the environment as easy-going as possible. I suggest, Mr. McCloskey, that we close it here and you proceed with your next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to number 17, Mr. Ruez's next image. It's a split image. Can you tell us, Mr. Ruez, what the photo on the left and right, they appear to be a joined image but can you tell us about them and what you're trying to express in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is a photograph I took in April 1997, the date is bottom right of the picture. This is why I recall precisely. It shows the intersection of Konjevic Polje at that date, intersection that you can see at the right of the picture, and again, the yellow arrow, this picture being taken from the bottom of the hill that we saw on the previous picture, indicates the rough direction that most of the people were trying to take in order to get out of this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you just orient us to this, if we could put the little cursor, what direction is the little hand in?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The top of the picture is the direction north towards Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And now let's go over here where there is another street. Where does that road go to the rite of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Middle right of the right photograph it goes from the intersection of Konjevic Polje towards Kravica and Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is this also one of those non-65 ter images? Or Mr. Bourgon, do you know, can you help us there? Without obstructing?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Unfortunately, Mr. President, we can't tell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So again, this would be marked for identification only for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, my recollection is there are several photographs of the intersection of Konjevic Polje both from the air and the ground and this identical one may not be there but that's -- that's the way I have interpreted actually it has a 65 ter number of 1617, but that's the kind of thing where I have interpreted photos differently from my colleague, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I believe that you made a very sensible suggestion which was to put these photos on a CD-ROM which could be disclosed to the Defence. I do not challenge the fact that we were given this by the Prosecution. I can't find it that's the problem. So when we come to cross-examination, we can't make reference to that photo, you see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's, as said, it's not only your problem, it's also our staff's problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, she is mistaken. This is on a CD-ROM.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But there one happens to be but the only way you can refer to it is number 17 out of 271. That's the only way you can refer to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's the problem. She has had -- but not the problem she stated. She has had this on a CD-ROM a very neat -- much better than we were able to provide the old Krstic and Blagojevic exhibits. They are neat with an index of where they are taken from and what they are from. This is a better product. I apologise for not having 65 ter numbers or having a motion to give them 65 ter numbers. I will always endeavour to do that. I'm not aware that the intersection of Konjevic Polje was a contested matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But Mr. McCloskey, anything can become highly contested in a trial. And without prior notice. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. President the issue is not whether the intersection of Konjevic Polje is contested or not. That is not the issue. The issue is in this case my colleague from the Prosecution says in this case we have a number it's number 1616 or 16 whatever number they gave out. Now, I brought this issue to the attention of my colleague many days ago. Why can he just simply go through the 271 pictures and just tell us what numbers those are? This would be so easy and then we would know how many of those pictures are not or are new and then we could at least limit the debate to those new pictures and it will be much easier. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President could I remind you of what I've responded to that in the -- I have done that. With the help of some people, we went through all 270 and we compared those to the Blagojevic/Krstic items. Many we found were either the same or very close and many we found were photos of -- but from a different angle or different quality and the only one that I recall that I didn't find a clear one of was these picture of the mountains but we have got pictures of the mountains on the Petrovic film that you just saw. Those are the same mountains. It's a little bit farther down. We have got aerial images of this whole thing. If we go through and track and try to connect these identically, that I mean that's going to take a very long time but they are the same or similar. We can do that, of course. We'll do that if it will help resolve the issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's clarify it even further because I mean, what you both say has a lot of validity in it but at the same time, we have a responsibility to make sure that the rules are applied as much as possible. So what we are going to state or to decide is the following: Namely that we take it that having already reviewed these 271 images, you should be in a position to identify those which have a 65 ter meeting -- ter number, 65 ter number. So what you are required to do is you don't need to do it now or by tomorrow but please do it at ASAP, make available a list of these images with cross-references to the 65 ter so that we would know that image number 17, for example, has 65 ter -- is equivalent to document with 65 ter number 1619 or whatever number you mentioned. Any other image that you cannot identify, then that will remain throughout the entire testimony of this witness until we finish with P02103 as marked for identification purposes only. At the end, we then will decide whether the entire P02103 should be entered into the records as a separate exhibit, in which case we will also give instructions on how this should be done, at least accompanied by a more comprehensive statement or list, descriptive list of the various images it contains. Does that -- is that fine with you? Does it allay further your preoccupations, which are also our preoccupations, Mr. Bourgon? Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We will get that do done this weekend, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you for your cooperation. We will proceed and have a break at 12.30 or at any time soon are or later as you prefer, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think we've exhausted the intersection of Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If there is something else you wanted to point out on this, Mr. Ruez, that you wanted to communicate?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We gave the direction of Zvornik, we gave the direction of Bratunac but we have not given the direction of Nova Kasaba which is at the left of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Where the cursor is. Thank you very much. I missed that third important direction. Okay. Let's go to 18. Now, you entitled this map as prisoners of war regroupment sites, 13 July. What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this map is showing all the areas where witnesses have told us that they had been detained so we'll -- it's an introduction to then show you every area one by one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I just noticed that we have the witness is referring to a term called prisoners of war. Mr. President, we mentioned this in our pre-trial brief. Prisoners of war is a term that exists only in the context of an international armed conflict. It does not exist in the body of law that replies to a non-international armed conflict. In this case the Prosecution has not specified which type of conflict we are dealing with so I would appreciate if we could refrain from using terms that are specifically applied to international armed conflict. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you wish to respond to that, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I thank you, Mr. Bourgon for having raised this matter, which would have been -- which would have carried a lot of weight and would have been an extremely important submission if we had a panel of jurors here but we know the law and international law, let's say, at least as any one of you and let's proceed. I don't think this is going to change anything. We know exactly what the witness is referring to and if he has referred to them as prisoners of war, it doesn't mean that we are considering them as prisoners of war or that we agree with him that they are prisoners of war and that they should be prisoners of war. That can become a matter of an ad hoc submission later on if either of the parties wish to make such, but for the time being, we are understanding this to mean referring to Muslim detainees. Yes, Mr. McCloskey, first, and then Mr. Ostojic. So it's not a question of size, it's a question of I think I should -- we should first hear your response.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We agree this is not meant to have any legal significance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right I apologise to you for having basically decided this without -- well, actually we asked you and you decided not.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour on page 38 line 16 and the witness has repeatedly throughout his testimony referenced using the words "we" and as he does here where he says, "where witnesses have told us," if he's a specific witness I would like if possible so we don't have to go back to this ad nauseam in our cross, if he's can simply tell us if he's done it or if he's done it in cooperation with someone else. It may shorten some of the cross questions but even this picture he says, "We have pin pointed this from witnesses that have shared it with us." Who is the us? If it's the Office of the Prosecutor then we wouldn't have to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're perfectly right. I don't think I need to explain to you, Mr. Ruez, if you wish or you prefer to continue referring to "us" and "we," et cetera, perhaps you could be specific as to who you are referring to apart from yourself.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you tell us who you've been referring to?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, first of all regarding the issue of the prisoners of war label, I take full responsibility for this. I didn't double check that with the Prosecution. Regarding the fact that I often say, I mean, more or less always say "we" in fact it's a French judicial police habit where even when you do something alone, you refer to the result or to the action as the one of a collective group. So I will as much as possible say "I" when I am the person. When I say information was provided to us, I mean to the investigation team that existed at the time, and I will -- I might say "with me," if you wish, since the investigators in the team then reported the results of what they learned to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I would take it in addition, Mr. Ruez, that the investigation teams varied because we are talking of a long, rather long, period of time. You were there investigating so I take it that the investigation team was not always the same, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was not unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I also take it, Mr. Ostojic, that you are not really interested in particular names. If you are, then we would need to address that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Not at this time yet, Your Honour, but there may come a time, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey. Thank you, Mr. Ostojic and thank you, Mr. Ruez, for your explanation. Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If it appears there is something very specific that may be contested, I will tend to ask the witness to give us his source. I may be wrong on what's contested but I will go ahead and do our best.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Ruez, then, we have seen that you have marked in these little blue-green circles the various spots we see their names and so I guess let's just we'll go through them one at a time and talk about the photographs. So let's go to the next one, 19. And perhaps you can explain, we see on 19 we see Luke kind of off the map. Can you explain that briefly?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The spot of Luke is off the map because the map was not large enough to show that area but my assessment is that it's more or less accurate on this map. It is just before Kladanj that was the confrontation line. And Luke is the name of an elementary school located there, just before the drop off of the population that was transported there by bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 20. What is 20 depict?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exhibit 20 depicts the school known as being the elementary school of Luke.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what is the significance of this school, briefly to the investigation?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The significance is that one person who managed to get on board of a bus in Potocari, once arrived at the dropping zone, was separated from the women and the children, and taken with other prisoners to that school where he was then detained.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you give us the 65 ter number of that witness?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's not on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Some days -- okay.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, yes, number 54.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And how did you find this school?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We found it according to his indications since he had told us that he had walked a couple of hundred metres in the opposite direction of Kladanj, once he was singled out at the exit of the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And from this picture, which direction would be that drop off spot that we've seen in the previous videos?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: A few hundred metres if we would continue walking on the road in the direction shown by the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next shot. And is this the same building?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And from where?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a view from the rear of the building and I took this picture due to the fact that the witness said he had sat with a group in the first moment under the tree. This picture was taken in presence of the witness 54.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next photograph. What's this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The witness 54, when we were on that -- at that school indicated that he was then detained inside this classroom where he was beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 23. Okay. And we are changing locations now. Where are we going to next?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is another area where we have knowledge, people have been detained. The first one I will talk about is Nova Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to that next. We are at page 24. We have another aerial imagery. It's a United States aerial imagery dated 13 July with the title that we see. It also has a sort of a squiggly mark and 1400 hours. I think we've seen that before. What does United States -- what does that mean with the United States will allow you to say?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means that it is an approximate timing. It is not a precise timing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And can you -- you identified some buildings. What's the significance of that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is the facility of the 65th Protection Regiment. We know -- I mean, I know from what I heard from Dutch witnesses that detainees were brought to this compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, let me just keep going. We'll hear from those Dutch witnesses. And I've noticed that you've marked something as buses; is that right? Why have you marked that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because they are three buses on the parking lot of the -- this compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Let's go to the next shot. This is a -- number 25, a ground level shot. What is this of?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is a picture that I took in April 1996, again the date is at the bottom right of the photograph, and this shows the main building of the facility of the 65th Protection Regiment seen from the road at Nova Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 26. Another US imagery shot. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is an aerial imagery showing the area of Nova Kasaba on 13 July 1995, approximate hour 1400 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now you've seen Nova Kasaba from the air, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Does this -- is this a fair depiction of Nova Kasaba from the air as you know it?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a very precise picture on which we can see also buses on the road and the main point of this photograph is the area squared by trees at the top of the picture and this is a second detention place at Nova Kasaba, that is the soccer field.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you receive information on the investigation that people were placed on that soccer field on this date?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember having interviewed one person during the summer 1995, and on this photograph we will see it on a closer shot, we have been told that all the little dots that are on this soccer field are -- is a mass of prisoners -- I mean, of people standing on the soccer field or sitting on the soccer field.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to that next shot to explain that answer. Who -- where did you get that information from, that these dots were people?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not get that, I think, from the providers, because they did not mark it on the picture, but aside the source that I mentioned as being a witness interviewed in summer 1995. There is also another source who confirmed that later, and who was in the Bosnian Serb army at the time of the events.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next shot. And this is 28. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So the square in the middle is a group of people lined on the football field. One can see a few dots little bit south of that first group. And at the left, the long rectangle is also supposed to be a group of people

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, this is a US imagery shot and it says, "people at football field." So is that information provided by the United States?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in fact I didn't want to say it because I was not 100 per cent sure but Madeleine Albright who was US ambassador at the United Nations showed some aerial imagery from that area and the conclusion was that the people who were on this soccer field were then related with other photographs shown from the area of Nova Kasaba that showed disturbed soil.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's keep away from Madeleine Albright and the UN, if we can. And it might be a good time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But not before hearing what Mr. Bourgon has to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. At transcript page 45, lines 13 and 14, the witness mentioned a source who was in the Bosnian Serb army at the time of the events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I would just like to obtain confirmation whether these are witnesses who will appear in this trial and more information as to who these people are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Very valid question. The witness hasn't told us who this person is. I don't know whether you are aware who this person is and, if you are aware, you can answer the question straight away. If you're not, we will then need to maybe go into private session for a while, get the name, and then you would be able to tell us whether he's a prospective witness or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't recall, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But you will understand that this is a very relevant and important question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It may be simpler just to withdraw that and go on the evidence that we have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic? Not necessarily because that person eventually will turn up as a witness here can be confronted with a question which would relate precisely to the information that he may have given to Mr. Ruez. Yes, Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, with all due respect, there is actually two sources he mentioned he says first one source and then he specifically says another source who was in the army so it's both sources. I don't want to limit it to one. And it's this kind of testimony that we would just ask the Court if possible that they can clarify the issue so we don't have to revisit his testimony line by line during our cross-examination. He mentions two sources. He has a list with him that he can refer to and he should just simply tell us who the sources are. I believe that and I would ask that the Court instruct the Prosecution to follow-up on those specific questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Let's take that up immediately after the break. Indeed you are right, Mr. Ostojic. He does refer to one person being a witness interviewed in summer 1995 so a witness I take it witness -- witness means witness in a trial, to answer in some kind of proceedings, and then the other one, another source, who confirmed that later and who was in the Bosnian Serb army at the time of the events. Let's take that up straight away after the break. And Mr. Ruez, in the meantime I would like you to think about whether the mentioning of these names should be made in open session or in private session. I think you know better than any of the rest of us. You know who you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It will be even I think useless to go in private session because the person interviewed in July 1995 and then to who I refer to as being a witness, for me he's a witness of events. I don't take it in the sense witness in the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know there is no basis for her to be called for this trial so I believe she is not on any witness list. Also, the only witness list I have with me is the few names of those that we call the survivors of mass executions, not survivors of the events. I could for sure find the name of the witness I'm referring to and we have a statement of her in the records. But I don't have her name in the head.
